main_text.p: glia forte vel Gallia id eveniat, non alibi similiter, facillime judicabit, qui judicium adhibuerit. Sunt equidem & vigent alibi locorum confimiles in rebus aliis luperstitiones seu abominationes, eaque diversis in locis diversæ. Ita (pródolor!) in hac regione, atque in tractu vicino, nondum penitus animis mortalium exempta superstitiosa illa origo ac curatio affectus, quem Man-flacht appellant, (de quo alibi egi peculiari Tractatu,) in quo sane superstitio effectum horrendum non raro fortitur, at non nisi apud eos, qui superstitioni sunt dediti. Ita multis perfuafum est, ac respondet Experientia, si puerpera quem videat, vel audiat duntaxat vocem alicujus, qui olim forte homicidium patravit, quamvis neficiat ipsa id unquam patratum, incidere miseram in horrenda symptomata prædicti affectus; ac si modo idem qui patravit homicidium, illi puerperæ propinet hauftulum potus, five vini,.
main_text.notes: Catchword and signature absent. The running head is read as "Sympathetico"; the page number as printed "615" (the scan shows "615" with a damaged digit). Several words in the first lines are slightly blurred; "superstitiones" for "luperstitiones" and similar readings are uncertain. The Germanic word "Mannflacht" is printed in black letter and is shown here in italics as "Man-flacht", which is doubtful.
